title: 2017 Tax Act Initially Projected to Add $1.46 Trillion to Deficit; Top 1% Gets 83% of 2027 Benefit
description_medium: President Donald Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act on December 22, 2017. It cut the corporate rate from 35% to 21% and changed individual rates and deductions. The initial CBO and Joint Committee on Taxation estimate projected a net $1.46 trillion deficit increase over 2018–2027. A later CBO estimate put the broader effect, including macroeconomic feedback and debt-service costs, at about $1.9 trillion over 2018–2028. Tax Policy Center estimated that the top 1% would receive 83% of the law’s total tax benefit in 2027.
description_long: President Donald Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act on December 22, 2017. It reduced the federal corporate income-tax rate from 35% to 21% and changed individual rates, deductions and other provisions. The initial Congressional Budget Office and Joint Committee on Taxation score projected a net deficit increase of about $1.46 trillion over fiscal years 2018–2027, after accounting for reduced outlays that partly offset the revenue loss. CBO later estimated a broader $1.9 trillion increase over 2018–2028 after including macroeconomic feedback and debt-service costs. Those figures use different periods and accounting assumptions. Separately, the Tax Policy Center estimated that in 2027 the top 1% of households would receive 83% of the law’s total tax benefit for that year. That distribution estimate reflects the scheduled expiration of most individual provisions after 2025; by 2027, the remaining average tax reduction was small and more concentrated among high-income households. The 83% estimate should not be applied to earlier years or treated as the top 1% share over the law’s full duration. These are projections of tax and budget effects under the law’s original terms.

corrected_wording.original_claim: CBO projected a $1.9 trillion conventional deficit increase over 2018–2027, before interest.
corrected_wording.corrected: The initial CBO/JCT estimate was a net $1.46 trillion increase over 2018–2027. CBO later estimated about $1.9 trillion over 2018–2028 including macroeconomic feedback and debt-service costs.

source_access_notes: Verified the initial $1.455T CBO/JCT estimate, CBO’s later $1.854T broader estimate including macroeconomic feedback and debt service over 2018–2028, and TPC’s 83% 2027 distribution figure. The two deficit estimates are now explicitly distinguished by period and basis.
rationale: Aligns the deficit wording with CBO’s original score and subsequent broader estimate, eliminating ambiguity with the separate entry on the $1.46T initial score.
